Hello! I am using gulp-eslint (latest) and babel-eslint (latest) when check codestyle.

My code:

```
  /**
   * @param {Object} locator
   * @param {Object} context
   * @param {String} id

   * @param {Function} output
   */
  function sync ({ locator, context, id }, state, output) {

  }
```

ESLint Error:

57:2  warning  Expected JSDoc for 'state' but found 'context'   valid-jsdoc
57:2  warning  Expected JSDoc for 'output' but found 'id'       valid-jsdoc

body:
@nzakas,
The fix in a1da3b4 sort of dodges the issue a bit, and doesn't quite do what we'd hope it could…

It turns out JSDoc does support destructing via making up a placeholder name. It is lacking in official documentation.
https://github.com/jsdoc3/jsdoc/issues/987

``` js
/**
 * @param {object} param
 * @param {number} param.a - First value
 * @param {object} param.b - Wrapper
 * @param {number} param.b.c - Second value
 * @return {number} sum a and b
 */
letters = ({a, b: {c}}) => a + c;
```

Perhaps, we can support this kind of grammar?

The following doesn't work either:

``` js
/**
 * @param {object} a - First value
 */
letters = ({a} = {}) => a;
```

body:
As pointed out by @mattyclarkson eslint has trouble with a default value for destructured params

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1134683/15130656/c6e396f2-160f-11e6-8157-391b8131e488.png)

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1134683/15130808/c6d04092-1610-11e6-8f9b-f3324c4ae642.png)

It seems like this is a good behavior. Using destructuring in a method or function signature seems like a poor contract to make. 

I would suggest that it is a good practice to have all required items listed separately in the method signature and use a single parameter for a config object. 

Within the function body, it makes sense to use destructuring to pull out distinct properties from the provided config/options object. And it would make sense to use destructing when calling the method. But I don't think destructing belongs in the method signature itself.
